description: This chart illustrates five distinct layer grouping patterns, comparing the distribution of layers across four groups. The horizontal axis represents the group categories (G1, G2, G3, G4), while the vertical axis represents the number of layers in each group, with no explicit label or units provided. Each pattern is depicted as a set of four bars, colored in various shades of green, with the height of each bar corresponding to the number of layers in that group. The "Increasing" pattern shows a gradual increase in layer count from approximately 0.25 to 1.25, while the "Uniform" pattern displays consistent heights across all groups, at roughly 0.75. The "Decreasing" pattern mirrors the "Increasing" pattern, with the tallest bar on the left and decreasing heights to the right, ranging from approximately 1.25 to 0.25. The "Spindle" pattern has the tallest bar in the middle, with heights decreasing towards the edges, ranging from approximately 0.25 to 1. The "Bottleneck" pattern has the shortest bar in the middle, with the outer bars being the tallest, at around 0.75. The bars within each pattern are not labeled or sorted in a specific order, and no visual emphasis is placed on any particular bar.
